question.text: A put option has a delta of -0.4. If the underlying moves up by Rs. 20, what happens to the put premium?

explanation.text: The Logic: Change in option price = Delta × Change in underlying Step-by-step: 1. Delta = -0.4 2. Change in underlying = +Rs. 20 3. Change in put premium = -0.4 × 20 = -Rs. 8 4. Negative sign = premium DECREASES The Trap: Put delta is NEGATIVE. When underlying goes UP, put premium goes DOWN. Cross-Exam Context: Put delta: -1 to 0. Negative because puts move opposite to underlying. Distributor's Pro-Tip: Put premium change = (-0.4) × 20 = -Rs. 8. Put loses value when stock rises.
